title: Signed-writing clause vs requested extras
signal: The buyer orally asks for extras, gets them, then refuses to pay only because no signed writing exists.
student_move: Cut timing and consideration doctrines; then use the Gold Key to kill the condition defense.
tiny_rule: Requested-and-performed extras can defeat a signed-writing-only defense.
trap: The condition label feels exact because the writing clause really exists.

title: Purpose Gate for Parol Evidence
signal: Complete integration plus outside negotiations.
student_move: Ask what the evidence is being used to do.
tiny_rule: Interpret ambiguity can come in; add or contradict terms cannot.
trap: four-corners absolutism

title: Source of the missing term
signal: Written goods contract is silent; choices offer trade practice, oral words, business harm, and competitor conduct.
student_move: Cut actor/effect facts; clash the two source facts.
tiny_rule: Trade usage can be a UCC source of meaning; prior oral contradiction is not the same source.
trap: Direct word-match to 'exclusive.'

title: Supervening illegality — mistake vs impracticability
signal: A federal criminal statute takes effect between offer and acceptance, unknown to both parties, and the contract performance has become illegal.
student_move: Resolve formation first (revocation needs receipt; rejection needs receipt; acceptance is dispatch). Then apply the Gold Key: the NCBE framed key is mutual mistake; impracticability is co-credited.
tiny_rule: When a supervening criminal statute triggers, both mutual mistake and supervening impracticability may discharge; the NCBE's framed key is mutual mistake.
trap: The dominant trap is the most-picked answer (impracticability). It is doctrinally true; the discrimination is which framing the NCBE key picks.

title: Suretyship main-purpose gate
signal: If the borrower does not pay, I will.
student_move: Ask whether the guarantor was mainly seeking personal economic advantage.
tiny_rule: No self-benefit means oral guaranty stays in the writing-required bucket.
trap: no-consideration dominant trap and one-year bait

title: Protected-class statute beats violation-alone forfeiture
signal: The drafter invokes its own statutory omission against the protected buyer.
student_move: Cut wrong-frame answers first, then use the Gold Key on the violation-alone answer.
tiny_rule: The protected party may enforce when nonenforcement would frustrate the protective statute.
trap: Every statutory violation voids the deal.

title: Formation is not enforceability
signal: Oral goods deal over $500 with no writing and a missing price term.
student_move: Check the writing gate before rewarding the open-price rule.
tiny_rule: Open price can be filled, but the UCC writing gate still blocks enforcement unless an exception applies.
trap: Yes because open price does not defeat contract formation.

title: Mistake rescission: hidden main-use fact, no assumed risk
signal: A buyer wants rescission after a new fact appears.
student_move: Check direction, purpose, and risk.
tiny_rule: Hidden main-use defect can support rescission; known risks, side uses, and hidden upside do not.
trap: Treating any surprising post-sale fact as enough.

title: One-sided cancellation before performance
signal: A purchase order says one side may cancel at any time before the performance window.
student_move: Do not label it as an option first; ask whether that party made a real commitment.
tiny_rule: Unrestricted cancellation before performance makes that side’s promise illusory.
trap: Treating the one-sided escape hatch as a formed option contract.

title: Risk bucket beats surprise
signal: Specialist contractor, fixed price, required excavation, no testing, and moderate cost increase.
student_move: Ask who carried the risk before asking whether the surprise was mutual or expensive.
tiny_rule: Unknown subsurface conditions usually stay with the specialist contractor when the contractor had the chance to test and priced the job anyway.
trap: Mutual-mistake and impracticability answers that omit assumption of risk.

title: Same debt later is not new consideration
signal: fixed and undisputed debt already due
student_move: Ask what new thing the debtor gave for the creditor’s no-suit promise.
trap: bargain language hides the missing new exchange

title: NOT accurate + performance notice
signal: A negative call asks for the inaccurate statement in a unilateral credit-guaranty setup.
student_move: Invert the call first, then test the notice phrase against the performance-acceptance anchor.
tiny_rule: Performance can accept a unilateral offer, but notice can still matter when the offeror otherwise lacks a reliable way to learn that performance occurred.
trap: Picking an accurate contract rule because it sounds familiar.

title: Sub-bid recovery needs lock-in reliance
signal: Low sub-bid used in prime bid, then revoked before award.
student_move: Find the fact that shows the general contractor was locked into the prime bid.
tiny_rule: Lock-in beats mitigation.

title: Revocable is not revoked
signal: Unpaid option consideration plus later acceptance attempt
student_move: Separate option status from offer status.
tiny_rule: No option means the offer can be revoked; it does not mean the offer already ended.
trap: Treating failed irrevocability as automatic revocation.

title: Crossed writings: preserve the uncertainty
signal: Two matching writings cross and the call asks whether a contract already exists.
student_move: Do not force a clean acceptance story; ask whether the answer preserves the uncertain formation moment.
tiny_rule: Article 2 can recognize agreement even when no exact formation moment is identified.
trap: Treating identical cross-offers as an offer followed by acceptance.

title: Revocable is not revoked
signal: Merchant signed assurance longer than three months; acceptance after month three; no revocation fact.
student_move: Ask whether the seller actually revoked or whether the answer only says the offer became revocable.
tiny_rule: The firm-offer cap ends irrevocability only.
trap: Treating the cap as lapse.

title: Cancellation-window cutoff
signal: The buyer can cancel only before a named date and then does not cancel.
student_move: Mark the cancellation deadline, then ask what legal status exists after that date.
tiny_rule: A freely cancelable promise may stop being illusory when the cancellation window closes unused.
trap: Calling the missed deadline an option or a condition subsequent.

title: Promissory Estoppel Gate List
student_move: When reliance appears after a future gift promise, cut broad no-gift and invented-extra-gate answers.
tiny_rule: Gift promise plus reliance can be enforceable only if enforcement is needed to avoid injustice.

title: Requirements contracts are not blanks
signal: all needs, all requirements, all output, exclusive supply
student_move: Treat all-requirements language as the quantity term, then ask whether the disputed act breaks an actual contract term.
tiny_rule: All requirements is enough; good faith polices quantity.
trap: minimum-quantity myth and offer-revocation wrong frame

title: Exclusive output deal supplies best efforts
signal: Seller output plus buyer exclusivity in goods.
student_move: Do not demand an express buy-all sentence; ask whether exclusivity supplies the action promise.
tiny_rule: Exclusive dealing imposes best efforts to supply and promote unless otherwise agreed.
trap: Same-result market-risk answer and no-mutuality answer.

title: Contract lane before backup remedy lane
signal: The call says breach of contract and the stem gives a signed writing.
student_move: Cut promissory estoppel and unjust enrichment unless the contract lane is blocked.
tiny_rule: Use waiver when the protected party gives up a failed condition and the other side relies.
trap: Choosing the fairest-sounding payment theory instead of the contract concept.

title: Protected condition waiver
signal: One side says its own commitment depends on approval, but later wants to proceed anyway.
student_move: Ask whose protection the condition serves before treating nonoccurrence as a defense.
tiny_rule: The protected side can waive its own condition.
trap: Treating nonoccurrence as automatically fatal.

title: Beneficiary status does not beat a failed condition
signal: A nonparty sues on a promised benefit, but the stem emphasizes the promisee’s earlier failed performance.
student_move: Name the status-vs-defense axis before choosing the status answer.
tiny_rule: Third-party beneficiary rights remain subject to contract-level failed conditions and uncured material breaches.
trap: Picking the beneficiary label as if it ends the case.

title: Installment amount ladder
signal: The answer choices offer nothing, matured installments, and full balance.
student_move: Lock the date in the call and count what has matured before considering full-balance remedies.
tiny_rule: Due installments are collectible now; unmatured installments need an acceleration trigger.
trap: Upgrading a few missed payments into the whole balance.

title: Late specification is not automatically fatal
signal: goods sale leaves assortment or performance particulars for later
student_move: Ask whether the late choice materially affected the other party’s performance.
tiny_rule: No material effect means no refusal to perform.
trap: deadline language treated as an express condition

title: Installment Cure Beats Perfect Tender
signal: Goods due in separate dated lots plus prompt replacement promise.
student_move: Do not run ordinary perfect tender; run the installment matrix.
tiny_rule: A curable nonconforming installment with assurance must be accepted; canceling the whole contract requires substantial impairment of the whole.
trap: ordinary perfect-tender partial rejection

title: Act-as-repudiation vs self-created impossibility
signal: Promisor transfers the promised specific item before the date for performance.
student_move: Treat the transfer as the breach trigger, then cut excuses and tender-blame answers.
tiny_rule: Own-act inability is repudiation, not impossibility excuse.
trap: Impossibility language and tender language both distract from the seller's prior transfer.

title: Land-sale late tender: date breach is not automatic walkaway
student_move: Clash missed date against time-not-essential; then apply land-specific performance anchor.

title: Seller remedies: price is the exception
signal: Buyer rejects and returns conforming goods.
student_move: On a NOT-proper-measure call, separate price actions from damages formulas.
tiny_rule: Price requires acceptance, loss/damage after risk passed, or inability to resell.
trap: Treating contract price as ordinary expectation damages.

title: Delay in real-property possession — foreseeability of special costs
signal: Seller delays delivering possession; buyer wants both fair rental value and a special cost the seller did not know about.
student_move: Cut the wrong-frame and contradiction choices first; then use the Gold Key to strip any unforeseeable special cost from the additive choice.
tiny_rule: Fair rental value for the delay is recoverable; special costs are recoverable only if the seller knew of the buyer's particular needs at contracting.
trap: The additive choice packages the right base amount with a sympathetic extra cost.

title: Breacher restitution cap versus completion overrun
signal: Breaching performer sues for reasonable value and the nonbreaching party paid a replacement to finish.
student_move: Anchor the contract price first, then subtract amounts already paid and reasonable completion cost.
tiny_rule: The nonbreaching party should not pay more than the contract price for the promised completed performance.
trap: Netting unpaid reasonable value to the breacher.

title: Money promise is not an automatic no-SP answer
signal: Answer says a court will not specifically enforce a promise to pay money.
student_move: Treat the categorical no as suspect and ask whether damages are adequate.
tiny_rule: Specific performance turns on adequacy, not on a blanket money/non-money label.
trap: Confusing personal-service refusal with money-payment promises.

title: New business is not automatic no
student_move: When an answer or instruction says new-business profits are never recoverable, replace never with proved with reasonable certainty.
trap: dominant trap C

title: Remedy object before formula
signal: A remedies call follows a dense formation or option setup.
student_move: Name what the winner lost before calculating.
tiny_rule: If buyer wins on the land bargain, use fair market value of the property minus contract price.
trap: Students price the wrong object or treat specific performance's unavailability as nominal-only.

title: Future provider beneficiary
signal: pay whoever provides the item or service
student_move: Separate provider-intent from provider-knowledge.
tiny_rule: Intent creates beneficiary status; knowledge/reliance affects other issues.
trap: unnamed/unaware provider

title: Mailbox rule — proper dispatch and postal loss
signal: A mailed acceptance is lost or delayed; the question is whether a contract was formed.
student_move: Apply the Gold Key: the mailbox rule applies only when the acceptance is properly dispatched (correct address + correct postage). If the acceptance was properly dispatched, the rule applies; the post office's loss is irrelevant (Silver Key). If the acceptance was misaddressed or unstamped, the rule does not apply.
tiny_rule: Mailbox rule = acceptance effective on dispatch ONLY when properly dispatched (correct address + correct postage).
trap: The dominant trap is 'Yes, because the offeree mailed the acceptance' — it omits the properly dispatched element. The secondary trap is 'No, because the mail was lost' — it reverses the mailbox rule's allocation of postal risk.

title: Third-party beneficiary package deal
signal: A nonparty enforces a contract that also limits the claim.
student_move: Do not split the contract into benefit-only and cap-free pieces.
tiny_rule: TPB right travels with the contract terms.
trap: Nonparty status feels like freedom from the cap.

title: Requirements estimate is not a floor
signal: all requirements + estimate + shutdown
student_move: Stay in the quantity/good-faith lane before considering excuse or writing rules.
tiny_rule: Estimate guides policing; it is not automatically a minimum.
trap: Treating the estimate as the quantity promised.

title: Admission exception quantity cap
signal: No writing plus in-court admission of a smaller quantity.
student_move: Lock the admitted quantity before evaluating all-or-none answers.
tiny_rule: Admission opens enforcement only up to the quantity admitted.
trap: Some admitted contract means all alleged goods are enforceable.

title: Do not pay avoided costs.
signal: The stem gives contract price and expected cost, then says the contractor avoided all costs.
student_move: Subtract the avoided cost from the price.
tiny_rule: Expectation protects the net bargain, not the gross price.
trap: price/cost/zero answer array

title: Risk before rescission
signal: Mutual mistake plus as-is / unknown-defect clause.
student_move: Do not stop at both mistaken. Ask who took the risk.
tiny_rule: If the claimant accepted the mistake-risk, rescission is denied.
trap: Picking the mutual-mistake-only grant answer.

title: Accepted goods: notice keeps the remedy alive
signal: Buyer knows goods are defective, keeps silent, then raises defect after being sued.
student_move: Ask whether the buyer notified the seller within a reasonable time.
tiny_rule: Known defect plus no seasonable notice means no defect remedy after acceptance.
trap: Picking the nonconformity answer because the goods were genuinely defective.

title: Flexible quantity is not empty quantity
signal: all goods the buyer requires
student_move: Do not equate no fixed number with no quantity.
tiny_rule: Requirements quantity is measured by good-faith needs.
trap: Illusory-promise overread.

title: SOF memorandum: signer beats addressee
signal: A signed writing admits a guaranty but was sent to someone other than the enforcing creditor.
student_move: Map who is being sued; then ask whether that person signed a writing identifying the promise.
tiny_rule: The memorandum need not be addressed to the enforcing party.
trap: extra formality

title: Prospective inability: reliance before cure
signal: Future performance appears impossible, then later becomes possible.
student_move: Ask whether the other party changed position before the cure.
tiny_rule: Reliance before cure locks the defendant-side discharge.
trap: Later readiness feels decisive, but it is late.

title: Unless-trigger cuts off duty
signal: Contract says 'remains effective unless' or similar.
student_move: Track the exact trigger and timing before defaulting to breach, impossibility, or substantial performance.
tiny_rule: If the terminating event happened, the duty is cut off.
trap: treating initial effectiveness as permanent

title: Complete beats consistent
signal: Signed writing says complete and exclusive; offered term came before signing.
student_move: Do not ask only whether the oral term conflicts; ask whether the writing is complete.
tiny_rule: Complete integration excludes prior consistent add-ons.
trap: Consistency trap

title: Specific performance for goods: find the uniqueness trigger
signal: Buyer asks for specific performance of a chattel.
student_move: Ask whether the object is unique or highly unusual; ignore merchant status and reciprocity.
tiny_rule: Unique/highly unusual goods can support buyer specific performance.
trap: Ordinary personalty damages default overstated into a never rule.

title: Merchant confirmation: oral objection trap
signal: Two merchants, oral goods deal, signed confirmation, oral objection.
student_move: Check whether the recipient sent written notice of objection within 10 days.
tiny_rule: Written objection required; oral objection is not enough.
trap: Treating any timely objection as enough.

title: Existing duty is not new consideration
signal: A party promises to do the same thing already owed.
student_move: Ask what new legal detriment appears in the later exchange.
tiny_rule: Already owed is not newly paid for.
trap: Promise-for-promise wording looks like consideration.

title: Mode-of-Acceptance Label Drill
signal: One party says “I will buy if you deliver,” and the other says “I will deliver.”
student_move: Ask what act the first statement required and whether that act has happened.
tiny_rule: Words promising future delivery are not the delivery itself.
trap: Calling the future promise an acceptance or commencement.
